## Why SOURCE_READY was retired

One word covered four different situations: a file nobody had found, a file the connector could name, a file on local disk, and a file whose content had been read. A queue built on it cannot answer which units could be worked on this afternoon, which is the only question the queue exists to answer.

| old | new | because |
|---|---|---|
| SOURCE_READY on a K5 PL06 row | SOURCE_BINARY_READABLE + BOUNDARY_CONFIRMED | the module DOCX is local and hash-verified and the unit's anchors resolve in it |
| SOURCE_READY on a K5 PL01-PL08 candidate row | SOURCE_BINARY_READABLE | the binary is readable but no frozen unit boundary exists for it |
| SOURCE_READY on a K3 row | SOURCE_LOCATED_BY_CONNECTOR, or SOURCE_CONTENT_READ where the PDF was actually read | no K3 binary is on local disk; text came through the connector |
| SOURCE_BLOCKED on the K2 row | SOURCE_LOCATED_BY_CONNECTOR | the file is located and identified; it is the binary that is not local, and 'blocked' hid that distinction |

**97.8 percent source-ready** is retired. It counted a located K2 monolith and 30 unmapped K5 candidates as ready. It was arithmetically correct and practically meaningless.
